With progress on vaccinations and strong policy support, indicators of economic activity and employment have continued to strengthen. Under the Fed’s 2020 shift to average-inflation targeting (Powell, Jackson Hole), keeping rates near zero and continuing asset purchases is consistent with forecast/makeup targeting frameworks in Svensson and Woodford (2003; 2004) and with maintaining credibility via the Taylor principle (Clarida). The contemplated taper is a form of forward guidance at the zero lower bound, while QE’s influence on the yield curve aligns with evidence that term premia and long rates transmit policy (Cochrane–Piazzesi). Still, elevated but “transitory” inflation and virus-related uncertainty argue for caution, echoing models stressing real-time uncertainty and policy trade-offs (Söderström, 2002; Wieland, 2000). Overall tone: moderately positive but risk-aware.
